crash.text: A crash is different: voting a dead member out needs a majority of the whole old view, and one of two is not a majority, so two members cannot survive a crash.

stop.text: A clean stop (Ctrl-C, or `destroy()`) leaves by a vote, so two members survive a clean stop.

restart.text: Run the same file again and it is the same node in its next life, its rows back before it has a socket.

plugs.text: Kill -9 a whole cluster and restore it from the disks: no `persisted` write is lost.

minority.text: Writes need a majority. On the minority side of a split, writes wait in one bounded buffer and go through when the split heals.

reads.text: Reads never wait: every node keeps serving its local copy, through a split and after it is voted out.

digests.text: Every node keeps one log per writer and heals gaps by comparing digests with its peers.

vote.text: Members join and leave by vote.

owner.text: Each row has one owner, and only the owner stamps writes to it.

lww.text: A cell keeps the record with the biggest stamp. Nothing merges.

persisted.text: `persisted` means a majority has it on disk.

fsync.text: Durability is explicit: `persisted` means a majority finished the fsync.

liar.text: one lying disk cannot fake a majority

deadwal.text: the kernel treats a failed WAL as DEAD thereafter

cable.text: both ends observe linkDown, exactly like a real cable cut

lie.text: the batch resolves, but its rows do not survive a crash

silence.text: it is the missing line that counts, not silence on a live one

harmless.text: Harmless: two paths delivered the same thing.

tombstone.text: A small marker of the deletion is kept for a while so an older, late-arriving change cannot bring the value back.

lease.text: A restore resumes AT the ceiling, so no seq can ever be issued twice across lives

twoalone.text: two members alone cannot vote a dead one out

killcmd.text: `kill -9 271607` from terminal 4 (the pid is on its screen)

samecmd.text: The same command again is the SAME member

addcmd.text: node server.ts 4804                       # a fourth member: members 4 on every screen

twocmd.text: node server.ts 4802                       # only two members; kill -9 one: the other stops, writable false

ctrlc.text: Ctrl-C and SIGTERM are a clean stop for every live instance, then the process exits 0.

ladder.text: `committed` means the owner stamped it. `replicated` means a majority of the view holds it. `persisted` means a majority has it on disk.

residual.text: a retry can still outrace the ORIGINAL commit's replication to the new owner
